angle: Official datasets and evaluation harnesses: LongMemEval (v1 original and Sept-2025 cleaned, plus LongMemEval-V2), LoCoMo (snap-research), and third-party harnesses (legacy mem0 evaluation/, mem0ai/memory-benchmarks, supermemoryai/memorybench, letta-leaderboard, MemoryAgentBench, BEAM, LoCoMo-Plus, locomo-audit). All facts come from reading raw source files, READMEs, HF API metadata and arXiv HTML. Nothing heavy ran locally and no benchmark dataset files were downloaded; only small scripts, JSON headers and one 21-row changelog CSV were fetched.

items.metric: Dataset composition: number of questions and question types
items.value: 500 questions in each file. question_type is one of single-session-user, single-session-assistant, single-session-preference, temporal-reasoning, knowledge-update, multi-session. Abstention is not a separate type: a question_id ending in '_abs' marks one of the 30 false-premise questions, which are drawn from the other types. Per-type counts (secondary but consistent across sources): SSU 70, SSA 56, SSP 30, MS 133, KU 78, TR 133.
items.denominator_exclusions: 500 includes the 30 _abs questions. From gbrain's 470-question breakdown (KU 72, MS 121, SSA 56, SSP 30, SSU 64, TR 127), the abstention questions fall as KU 6, MS 12, SSU 6, TR 6, SSA 0, SSP 0. This split is derived from a secondary source, not stated by the authors.
items.code_license: MIT (repo LICENSE; HF dataset tag license:mit)
items.notes: The 500 and the 30 abstention questions are primary (README and paper Sec 3). Per-type counts appear only in the paper's Figure 9 image; the numbers here come from SGMem arXiv 2509.21212, LycheeMemory V2 and the totals in mem0's released JSON (78/133/56/30/70/133).

items.metric: Haystack size per instance
items.value: S: about 115k tokens (Llama 3 tokenizer), about 40 sessions per README or about 50 per paper; built with max 80 filler sessions and enforce_json_length=115000. M: about 500 sessions, about 1.5M tokens. Oracle: evidence sessions only, and haystack_session_ids are not sorted by time.
items.notes: The README says S and oracle fit a 128k model but M is too long for long-context testing.

items.metric: Released file sizes (bytes) and provenance
items.value: longmemeval_s_cleaned.json 277,383,467; longmemeval_m_cleaned.json 2,737,100,077; longmemeval_oracle.json 15,388,478. Original deprecated repo xiaowu0162/longmemeval: longmemeval_s 278,025,796; longmemeval_m 2,745,274,681; longmemeval_oracle 15,388,478. The oracle file has the identical git/LFS oid in both repos (8e6e661d...), so it is unchanged. Cleaned repo created 2025-09-19.
items.notes: The HF viewer fails on this dataset: the 'answer' column mixes int and string (ArrowTypeError), so harnesses must str() the answers. The original HF repo is marked deprecated in favor of longmemeval-cleaned.

items.metric: What changed in the cleaned release
items.value: The official changelog sheet has 21 session-level rows covering 20 question IDs (60472f9c appears twice). Actions: 17 'session removed' and 4 'no action'. Issue types: 11 answer interference, 5 ambiguous reference (3 removed), 5 info leak without conflict (3 removed). Authors' notes: ambiguous reference and info leak 'might affect retrieval evaluation'; answer interference means 'answer probably changed by filler sessions by mistake'.
items.notes: The sheet does not say whether each removal applies to S, M or both; both files shrank (S by about 0.64 MB, M by about 8.2 MB). Effect: at most about 20 of 500 questions differ, so original-vs-cleaned scores are close but not strictly comparable. Could not verify per-file effects without downloading the data.

items.metric: Official QA metric: answer accuracy by LLM judge
items.value: Judge is gpt-4o-2024-08-06 via the OpenAI API, n=1, temperature 0, max_tokens 10. label = ('yes' in response.lower()), a substring test. There are 4 non-abstention templates: (a) SSU/SSA/multi-session: yes if the response contains the correct answer or all intermediate steps, no if only a subset; (b) temporal-reasoning: same, plus off-by-one day/week/month errors are not penalized; (c) knowledge-update: correct if the updated answer is present even alongside old information; (d) single-session-preference: rubric-based, need not cover all rubric points. Any id containing '_abs' uses a separate 'unanswerable question + explanation' template. Also allowed as judges: gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 and a local llama-3.1-70b-instruct, but print_qa_metrics.py asserts the judge is gpt-4o-2024-08-06.
items.artifacts: Writes <hyp>.eval-results-gpt-4o with per-question autoeval_label. The authors released no per-question baseline logs; key-expansion and timestamped-event caches are on Google Drive.

items.metric: Official aggregate definitions
items.value: Three numbers are reported: (1) Task-averaged Accuracy = unweighted mean of the 6 per-question_type accuracies; (2) Overall Accuracy = mean over all evaluated questions (500, including abstention); (3) Abstention Accuracy over the 30 _abs questions. Abstention questions are also counted inside their parent question_type buckets.
items.denominator_exclusions: No exclusions for QA: 500 including the 30 abstention questions.
items.notes: Third-party 'LongMemEval accuracy' numbers on 470 answerable questions, or task-averaged instead of overall, are not the same quantity.

items.metric: Agreement of GPT-4o judge with human experts
items.value: 30 questions per type. Judging GPT-4o answers: SSU 1.00, SSA 1.00, SSP 0.90, MS 1.00, KU 1.00, TR 1.00, ABS 0.97, average 0.98. Judging Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct answers: 0.97, 1.00, 0.97, 1.00, 1.00, 0.97, 0.90, average 0.97. The paper summarizes this as '>97% agreement'.
items.notes: Paper Table 6. The weakest agreement is on preference and abstention (open-ended responses).

items.metric: Official retrieval metrics and ID scheme
items.value: recall_any@k (any gold doc in top-k), recall_all@k (all gold docs in top-k) and ndcg_any@k, for k in {1,3,5,10,30,50}. Granularity is session or turn; turn runs also convert to session level by stripping turn ids and growing the effective k until k unique sessions are covered. Only USER turns are indexed: a session document is the user turns joined; the turn corpus is user turns only. Gold docs are corpus ids containing 'answer'. An answer session with no user turn marked has_answer=true is renamed 'noans', i.e. treated as non-gold. At turn level, gold = user turns with has_answer=true.
items.denominator_exclusions: The averages skip (a) all 30 '_abs' questions and (b) any question with no user-side has_answer turn ('Additionally ignored N instances'). N is printed at runtime, not published; it likely hits single-session-assistant questions whose evidence sits only in assistant turns (inference, not verified). The README states only the 30-abstention skip, which gives 470.
items.notes: print_retrieval_metrics.py prints only recall_all@5/@10 and ndcg_any@5/@10 (session) and recall_all@5/10/50 plus ndcg_any (turn). The paper's 'Recall@k' is therefore most likely recall_all (inference). Many third-party 'LongMemEval retrieval' claims report recall_any@5 on 470 with a user-only session index; that is a looser metric.

items.metric: Answer accuracy (GPT-4o judge, all 500)
items.value: No Chain-of-Note: oracle 0.870, S 0.606 (30.3% drop). With Chain-of-Note: oracle 0.924, S 0.640 (30.7% drop). Llama 3.1 70B with CoN: 0.848 oracle, 0.286 S.
items.reader: GPT-4o (and Llama 3.1 70B/8B, Phi-3/3.5 in the same figure)
items.budget: Full history in context (about 115k tokens for S)
items.notes: The commercial-system pilot (ChatGPT/GPT-4o 0.5773, Coze/GPT-4o 0.3299, offline reading GPT-4o 0.9184) used manual, much shorter histories and is not comparable to S.

items.system: LongMemEval paper: Stella V5 1.5B + fact-augmented keys
items.metric: Retrieval Recall@k / NDCG@k (paper's metric, likely recall_all) plus end-to-end QA accuracy
items.value: Value=session, K=V+fact: R@5 0.732, NDCG@5 0.620, R@10 0.862, NDCG@10 0.652; QA GPT-4o 0.714 top-5, 0.700 top-10. Value=round, K=V+fact: R@5 0.644, NDCG@5 0.498, R@10 0.784, NDCG@10 0.536; QA GPT-4o 0.657 top-5, 0.720 top-10. Plain value=session K=V: R@5 0.706, R@10 0.783.
items.reader: GPT-4o / Llama 3.1 70B / 8B with Chain-of-Note, json history format
items.budget: top-5 / top-10 retrieved items, sorted by timestamp
items.denominator_exclusions: Retrieval: skips abstention (and no-target) questions per code; QA: 500
items.notes: Table 3. Fact extraction by Llama 3.1 8B Instruct over user-side messages only. No per-question logs released.

items.benchmark: LongMemEval-V2 small / medium tiers, web + enterprise domains
items.metric: Benchmark definition and official harness settings
items.value: 451 manually curated questions, 5 abilities (static state recall, dynamic state tracking, workflow knowledge, environment gotchas, premise awareness), up to 500 multimodal web-agent trajectories per haystack, up to 115M tokens. Fixed reader Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B (temp 0.6, top_p 0.95, thinking on). Embeddings Qwen3-Embedding-8B. --memory-context-max-tokens defaults to 200,000. Judge gpt-5.2 with medium reasoning, used only for abstention (flawed-premise) and gotchas questions; other types use deterministic matchers (normalized phrase-set match, ordered match, multiple-choice letter match). Leaderboard score is LAFS gain over a fixed reference accuracy-latency frontier (accuracy = overall_full_set*100; latency = memory_query_avg_seconds). Submissions must include per_question.jsonl.
items.artifacts: Leaderboard packages require per_question.jsonl and run_args.json; the leaderboard showed 'entries coming soon' when fetched.
items.notes: arXiv 2605.12493 v1, 12 May 2026. Reported best: AgentRunbook-C 72.5% (abstract; tier not stated) vs RAG 48.5% and coding-agent baseline 69.3%. Project site: AgentRunbook-C 74.9% on the Small tier at 108.3 s average query latency. Split sizes per tier were not verified.

items.metric: Dataset composition
items.value: 10 conversations (a subset of 50 in the first arXiv release); locomo10.json is 2,805,274 bytes. QA per category: cat1 multi-hop 282, cat2 temporal 321, cat3 open-domain/commonsense 96, cat4 single-hop 841, cat5 adversarial 446, total 1,986. Evidence is a list of dia_ids formatted 'D<session>:<turn>' (e.g. 'D1:3'). Some entries are malformed or parenthesized; the official stats code strips '(' and ')'. Also included: generated observations and session summaries (gpt-3.5-turbo) and annotated event summaries. Images are not released; only URLs, BLIP captions and search queries.
items.notes: Category counts are secondary (mem0 memory-benchmarks prompts.py docstring and released JSON: 282/321/96/841 = 1,540; cat5 446 = 22.5% per locomo-audit), consistent with 1,986. The ID-to-name mapping is inferred from the official code: cat 2 gets the prompt 'Use DATE of CONVERSATION to answer with an approximate date' (temporal); cat 1 uses comma-split multi-answer F1 (multi-hop); cat 3 answers are split on ';' (open-domain).

items.metric: Official QA metric (not an LLM judge)
items.value: Normalization: lowercase, drop commas and punctuation, remove the words a/an/the/and. Tokens are Porter-stemmed. Cats 2, 3, 4: token F1 (cat 3 gold truncated at the first ';'). Cat 1: split prediction and gold on ',' and average over gold parts of the max F1 against any predicted part. Cat 5: score 1 if the prediction contains 'no information available' or 'not mentioned' (case-insensitive), else 0. The official aggregate (evaluation_stats.analyze_aggr_acc) averages over all 5 categories including cat 5.
items.denominator_exclusions: Official: none (1,986 including adversarial). Almost all third-party LLM-judge reports drop cat 5 and use 1,540.
items.reader: Official scripts: GPT-3.5/4, Claude, Gemini, HF models; full conversation truncated to the context window
items.notes: eval_recall/has_answer in the same file is an answer-string containment check over retrieved text, not evidence recall.

items.metric: Official evidence recall (turn-level, dia_id based)
items.value: recall = fraction of the question's evidence dia_ids present in the retrieved context ids. If the retrieved ids start with 'S' (session-summary database), matching is at session level. Questions with empty evidence are assigned recall 1. Defaults: --top-k 5, --retriever contriever; databases are dialogs, observations and session summaries.
items.notes: This is exact-ID evidence recall, suitable for HybridMind's evidence-ID contract. Watch the empty-evidence counted as 1 quirk and the malformed evidence strings.

items.metric: Known defect in the official cat-5 prompt construction
items.value: gpt_utils.py builds cat-5 multiple choice as '(a) Not mentioned in the conversation (b) {qa['answer']}' in random order. Adversarial rows store their distractor under 'adversarial_answer', not 'answer' (Letta's harness comment). locomo-audit reports the field is missing on 444 of 446 cat-5 questions.
items.notes: The code is primary. The missing-field count is secondary (locomo-audit) and was not verified here because that would mean downloading the data file.

items.metric: Ground-truth error rate and judge leniency
items.value: 99 of 1,540 (6.4%) gold answers judged wrong, giving an aggregate score ceiling of 93.57%. An EverMemOS-style LLM judge accepted 62.81% of intentionally wrong 'vague-but-topical' answers (10.61% for specific-but-wrong answers). Open-domain (n=96) needs a gap of 15+ points to separate two systems (Wilson 95% CI).
items.notes: Third-party audit (created 2026-02-18). The 62.81% concerns the EverMemOS judge prompt, not LoCoMo's official F1.

items.system: mem0 legacy evaluation/ (mem0ai/mem0, used for Mem0 paper arXiv 2504.19413)
items.metric: LLM-judge J score plus F1/BLEU-1
items.value: ACCURACY_PROMPT tells the judge to 'be generous': an answer that 'touches on the same topic as the gold answer' counts as CORRECT, and dates in a different format count if they refer to the same period. Judge gpt-4o-mini, temperature 0, JSON label. evals.py and llm_judge.py skip category 5 ('# Skip category 5'). F1 uses simple lowercase whitespace tokenization without stemming, unlike the official stemmed F1.
items.judge: gpt-4o-mini, generous single prompt, 10 independent judge runs (paper)
items.notes: The in-repo evaluation/ was retired on 2026-06-13 (commit 9315e30) in favor of mem0ai/memory-benchmarks and is now a git submodule. Legacy dataset link was a Google Drive folder (locomo10.json, locomo10_rag.json).

items.metric: Overall LLM-as-a-Judge J (mean ± 1 sd over 10 runs)
items.denominator_exclusions: Adversarial category excluded ('ground truth answers were unavailable')
items.budget: Memory tokens per query: Mem0 1,764; Mem0g 3,616; Zep 3,911; full-context 26,031
items.notes: Paper Table 2.

items.benchmark: LoCoMo10 (downloaded from snap-research raw URL), categories 1-4
items.metric: Binary LLM judge (CORRECT/WRONG), unified prompt for all categories
items.value: Rules: CORRECT if AT LEAST ONE gold list item appears; paraphrases and same-valence emotions count; dates within 14 days and durations within 50% count; 'ONLY mark WRONG if ZERO correct items'. With --with-evidence, the gold dia_id messages are injected and evidence may override the gold answer ('mark CORRECT even when the generated answer diverges from the gold'). Cat 3 gold truncated at ';'. Code defaults: answerer and judge gpt-5, top-k 200, cutoffs 10/20/50/200, categories 1,2,3,4. The README text says default gpt-4o.
items.notes: Much more lenient than the official F1 or the legacy mem0 judge, so scores are not comparable to Mem0-paper J.

items.system: Mem0 Platform v3 (memory-benchmarks README vs released artifacts)
items.metric: Answer accuracy (LLM judge). README headline vs per-question JSON on main
items.value: README (commit 4b61c5d, 2026-05-13): LongMemEval 94.4% (472/500) top-200 and 94.8% (474/500) top-50; LoCoMo 92.5% (1425/1540) top-200 and 91.8% (1414/1540) top-50. Released JSONs on main: LongMemEval top-200 93.4% (467/500, timestamp 2026-04-06), top-50 90.4% (452/500); LoCoMo top-200 91.56% (1410/1540). The README-update commit changed only README.md (16+/16-), so the headline numbers have no matching released per-question artifacts.
items.judge: gpt-5; custom harness judges, not the official LongMemEval evaluate_qa.py
items.budget: top-200 or top-50 memories to the answerer (ANSWERER_MEMORY_LIMIT=200)
items.artifacts: Per-question JSON released for the older runs only. LoCoMo JSON metadata has 'merged_from_questions' listing about 150 (top-200) or more (top-50) question IDs merged from re-runs.
items.denominator_exclusions: LME: 500 including abstention; LoCoMo: cat 5 excluded
items.cost_latency: LME JSON reports avg_search_latency_ms 0.0 and add latency 0.0, so latency was not measured.
items.notes: BEAM (README): 1M pass rate 70.1% (491/700), avg nugget score 0.641; 10M 50.5% (101/200), 0.413-0.486. OSS runs (GPT-5 answerer and judge, Qwen 600M embedder): 91.0% with GPT-5 extraction.

items.metric: Judge prompt and answer prompt characteristics
items.value: A single unified judge for all types, labelled 'adapted from' the official evaluate_qa.py but substantially looser: 'When in doubt, lean toward yes'; ranges containing the answer count; '8 months and 20 days matches 9 months'; any refusal matches an abstention answer. The answer-generation prompt contains benchmark-item-specific hints (e.g. 'Suica' travel card, 'TripIt' app, 'Sales Manager' vs 'Senior Sales Engineer' role mismatch) and the judge contains item-specific rules (e.g. 'Notes instead of chords are acceptable'). Ingestion: user+assistant pairs (CHUNK_SIZE=2) in chronological order.
items.notes: The prompts look tuned on test items (possible test-set leakage), so these numbers are not comparable to official-judge LongMemEval results.

items.metric: Judge routing and LoCoMo category mapping
items.value: The default judge prompts copy the official LongMemEval per-type wording but return JSON. Routing uses questionType substrings: 'abstention'/'adversarial' go to the abstention prompt. LongMemEval question_type never contains 'abstention' and the evaluate phase has no '_abs' handling, so the 30 LME abstention questions are judged with their parent type's prompt against the explanation text. The LoCoMo loader maps 1→single-hop, 2→multi-hop, 3→temporal, 4→world-knowledge, 5→adversarial. That contradicts the official code, where cat 2 gets the date hint (temporal), and contradicts mem0's mapping. Cat 5 is not excluded by default. Providers can override the judge prompt; the Zep provider swaps in the generous mem0-style 'touches on the same topic' judge.
items.judge: Selectable (-j gpt-4o, sonnet-4, gemini-2.5-flash, ...); answering model default gpt-4o
items.notes: Per-category LoCoMo numbers from memorybench are mislabeled relative to the official categories. Loader file: src/benchmarks/locomo/index.ts.

items.metric: 'Retrieval metrics' (hit@k, precision@k, recall@k, MRR, nDCG)
items.value: An LLM judges each of the top-k results (default k=10) as relevant or not given the question and gold ANSWER. Gold evidence IDs are not used. recallAtK = 1 if any result is judged relevant, else 0, so it is a hit rate. totalRelevant = max(1, relevantRetrieved), so nDCG's ideal is set by what was retrieved. MemScore is reported as a triple: accuracy% / avg search latency ms / avg context tokens.
items.budget: orchestrator search limit 10; supermemory provider default limit 30, threshold 0.3
items.notes: Not evidence recall. Not comparable to LongMemEval recall_any/recall_all or LoCoMo dia_id recall.

items.metric: Answer accuracy with a SimpleQA-style grader
items.value: 74.0% for a Letta filesystem agent on gpt-4o-mini, per the Letta blog of 2025-08-12. The grader is GRADER_TEMPLATE (CORRECT/INCORRECT/NOT_ATTEMPTED, SimpleQA style) called via OpenAI gpt-4.1 at temperature 0; score is 1 only for grade 'A'. Category 5 is skipped in _build_dataset.
items.reader: gpt-4o-mini agent with search_files/grep tools and tool rules; files chunked per session or SeCom segments (gpt-4o-mini segmentation)
items.judge: gpt-4.1 (from leaderboard/utils.py request_openai default); the blog does not name the judge
items.code_license: No LICENSE detected via GitHub API (404)
items.artifacts: No per-question outputs found in the repo
items.notes: The blog compares against Mem0's 68.5% graph variant, which used a different judge and prompt. The judge differs from mem0's, so this is not apples-to-apples.

items.metric: Benchmark definition and LME sub-task judge
items.value: LME(S*) re-packs LongMemEval_S into 5 long dialogues (about 355K tokens each, GPT-4o-mini tokenizer) with 300 questions. It is judged by gpt-4o using a verbatim copy of the official LongMemEval per-type and abstention prompts (llm_based_eval/longmem_qa_evaluate.py). Other tasks use substring_exact_match or exact_match; Recsys uses Recall@5. HF splits: Accurate_Retrieval 22 rows, Test_Time_Learning 6, Long_Range_Understanding 110, Conflict_Resolution 8. Paper total 2,071 questions. RAG chunk size 512 for LME(S*); 4096 for Mem0/Cognee/Zep/MIRIX.
items.notes: arXiv 2507.05257. The HF data was revised 2025-07-22/26, 2025-08-05 and 2025-09-29 (removed samples), so check which version a result used. S* scores are not LongMemEval_S scores.

items.metric: Benchmark definition and scoring
items.value: 100 conversations (128K: 20, 500K: 35, 1M: 35, 10M: 10) and 2,000 validated probing questions: 20 per conversation, 2 per ability, 10 abilities (abstention, contradiction resolution, event ordering, information extraction, instruction following, knowledge update, multi-session reasoning, preference following, summarization, temporal reasoning). Scoring is a nugget-based LLM judge (0 / 0.5 / 1 per nugget, averaged) for 9 abilities; event ordering uses Kendall tau-b after LLM event alignment.
items.judge: The LLM judge model is configurable; src/llm.py defaults to gpt-4.1-mini (not confirmed as the paper's judge)
items.code_license: Code MIT; BEAM data CC BY-SA 4.0 (HF Mohammadta/BEAM and Mohammadta/BEAM-10M)
items.notes: arXiv 2510.27246 (v1 31 Oct 2025, v2 21 Feb 2026). mem0's '700 questions' for 1M (35×20) and '200' for 10M (10×20) match this layout.

items.metric: Benchmark definition and judge
items.value: Adds a 6th 'Cognitive' category: cue dialogues and trigger queries stitched into randomly chosen locomo10 conversations as new sessions using time_gap. An LLM judge scores correct=1, partial=0.5, wrong=0 on constraint consistency; the quick-start uses gpt-4o-mini as both answerer and judge. The Cognitive split has 401 questions (secondary, per JustMem arXiv 2609.19877).
items.code_license: No license file (GitHub API license null); bundles locomo10.json, which is CC BY-NC 4.0
items.notes: arXiv 2602.10715 v1, 11 Feb 2026. Because stitching picks a random base conversation, the haystack depends on the seed; unified_input outputs are gitignored.

key_takeaways: The official LongMemEval QA judge is gpt-4o-2024-08-06 at temperature 0 with max_tokens 10 and a 'yes'-substring label, using 4 per-type prompts plus an abstention prompt (src/evaluation/evaluate_qa.py). The official aggregates are overall accuracy on all 500 (including the 30 _abs), a task-averaged accuracy (mean of the 6 type means) and abstention accuracy on 30. 'LongMemEval %' claims are only comparable if they say which of these they are and which judge and prompt they used.

Official LongMemEval retrieval indexes only user turns. It computes recall_any@k, recall_all@k and ndcg_any@k for k in {1,3,5,10,30,50} at session and turn level, and skips the 30 _abs questions plus any question with no user-side has_answer turn. The paper's Recall@k is most likely recall_all. Third-party 'retrieval 98%' claims usually mean the much looser recall_any@5 on 470. For HybridMind: report both metrics with exact session and turn IDs, and compute and log the no-target exclusion count from the data.

The Sept-2025 cleaned release is small and auditable. The changelog has 21 rows over 20 question IDs (17 sessions removed, 4 no action), the oracle file is byte-identical, and the S and M files shrank slightly. Results on the original and cleaned S differ on at most about 20 questions. Record which file was used (the HF answer column mixes int and str).

The official LoCoMo metric is not an LLM judge. It is Porter-stemmed token F1 (comma-split partial F1 for cat 1, gold truncated at ';' for cat 3) plus a keyword check for cat 5, averaged over all 1,986 questions. Evidence recall is exact dia_id ('D<session>:<turn>') coverage, with empty-evidence questions counted as 1. Nearly all vendor numbers instead use an LLM judge on cats 1-4 (1,540), and the data is CC BY-NC 4.0.

Category mapping is not standardized. Official code and mem0 use 1=multi-hop, 2=temporal, 3=open-domain, 4=single-hop, 5=adversarial. supermemory's memorybench maps 1=single-hop, 2=multi-hop, 3=temporal, 4=world-knowledge, so its per-category LoCoMo numbers are mislabeled. The official cat-5 formatter reads qa['answer'] while adversarial rows use 'adversarial_answer'.

Judge leniency drifts upward across harnesses: official LME per-type prompts → legacy mem0 'be generous, touches on the same topic' (gpt-4o-mini) → mem0 memory-benchmarks (partial credit from one item, 14-day date tolerance, 50% duration tolerance, 'lean toward yes', optional evidence overriding gold). mem0's LME answer and judge prompts contain item-specific hints (Suica, TripIt, 'notes instead of chords'), which suggests test-set tuning. locomo-audit found that 6.4% of LoCoMo gold answers are wrong (ceiling 93.57%) and that a judge accepted 62.81% of deliberately wrong vague answers.

mem0's current README headlines (LME 94.4%/94.8%, LoCoMo 92.5%/91.8%) come from a README-only commit. The per-question JSONs released on main show 93.4% (467/500) and 90.4% (452/500) for LME and 91.56% (1410/1540) for LoCoMo. The LoCoMo JSON also records merged re-run question lists, and latency fields are 0.0.

memorybench's retrieval 'recall@k' is an LLM-judged hit rate (1 if any top-10 result is judged relevant to the gold answer), not evidence recall. It cannot be compared to LME recall_any/recall_all or LoCoMo dia_id recall. It also judges LME abstention questions with non-abstention prompts because it never checks '_abs'.

Newer benchmarks shift the protocol. LongMemEval-V2 (Apache-2.0; 451 questions; up to 115M tokens; fixed Qwen3.5-9B reader; a gpt-5.2 judge only for abstention and gotchas, deterministic matchers otherwise) requires per_question.jsonl and scores accuracy against measured query latency (LAFS). BEAM (code MIT, data CC BY-SA 4.0; 100 conversations and 2,000 questions up to 10M tokens) uses nugget 0/0.5/1 judging plus Kendall tau-b. MemoryAgentBench's LME(S*) is 5 contexts of about 355K tokens with 300 questions and uses the official LME prompts with gpt-4o. LoCoMo-Plus adds a 401-question Cognitive split with 1/0.5/0 judging and has no license file.

Nothing was run locally. No benchmark dataset files were downloaded, only small scripts, JSON headers and the 21-row changelog CSV, and no provider calls were made. Unverified items are marked: per-type LME counts and the abstention split (secondary), the count of LME no-user-target questions, LoCoMo per-category counts (secondary via mem0 and the audit), BEAM's judge model, Letta's license, and the LME-V2 tier sizes.
